subsystems.name: Scanning tip assembly
subsystems.role: the 'pen' that picks up and places individual atoms.
parts: atomically sharp metal tip (tungsten or platinum-iridium)

subsystems.name: Vacuum and cryogenic environment
subsystems.role: keeps the workspace free of contaminants and reduces thermal motion.
parts: liquid helium or mechanical cooling to a few kelvin

subsystems.name: Atom source and delivery
subsystems.role: provides the atoms to be placed.

subsystems.name: Control and feedback electronics
subsystems.role: measures tunneling current and controls tip position with sub-atomic precision.

subsystems.name: Substrate and assembly stage
subsystems.role: the surface on which atoms are arranged.
parts: atomically flat substrate (e.g., copper or silicon)

subsystems.name: Characterization and metrology
subsystems.role: verifies the structure atom by atom.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the vacuum environment
buildSteps.detail: Assemble an ultra-high vacuum chamber with pumps and bakeout heaters to reach pressures below 10⁻¹⁰ mbar, so that atoms stay clean for hours.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the tip
buildSteps.detail: Electrochemically etch a tungsten or platinum-iridium wire to a single-atom apex, then clean it in vacuum by heating or field evaporation.

buildSteps.title: Build precision positioners
buildSteps.detail: Install a piezoelectric tube scanner for sub-nanometre motion and a coarse stage for millimetre travel, all mounted on a vibration-isolated platform.

buildSteps.title: Wire the control loop
buildSteps.detail: Connect the tip to a current amplifier and feedback electronics that adjust the tip height to keep the tunneling current constant, enabling atomic-scale positioning.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the substrate
buildSteps.detail: Cleave or sputter-anneal a metal or semiconductor crystal to expose an atomically flat surface, then cool it to a few kelvin to suppress diffusion.

buildSteps.title: Load the atom source
buildSteps.detail: Set up an evaporator or gas doser to deposit atoms onto the substrate or directly onto the tip, with a shutter to control dose.

buildSteps.title: Manipulate atoms
buildSteps.detail: Approach the tip to the surface, then use voltage pulses or tip-atom forces to pick up, move and place individual atoms one at a time.

buildSteps.title: Assemble layer by layer
buildSteps.detail: Repeat pick-and-place operations to build the desired structure, imaging after each step to detect and correct misplaced atoms.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: For practical objects, develop parallel tip arrays or hybrid schemes that combine atomic placement with self-assembly to place many atoms simultaneously.

prerequisites.why: invented in 1981, it provides the ability to image and manipulate individual atoms on a surface.
demonstrated for small numbers of atoms, but only in laboratory settings and at very low temperatures.
needed to keep atoms clean and still, and to prevent unwanted chemical reactions.
current methods are serial and extremely slow, placing only a few atoms per second at best.
STM can image atoms but cannot quickly characterize bulk materials or detect subsurface defects.
no method exists to correct millions of placement errors across a macroscopic object.

pathway.milestone: individual atoms arranged into patterns and letters in ultra-high vacuum at a few kelvin
pathway.unlocks: fundamental understanding of atom-by-atom construction and quantum effects.

pathway.milestone: parallel tips or arrays of STM tips to increase throughput
pathway.unlocks: creation of small, perfect nanostructures for quantum devices and catalysts.

pathway.milestone: hybrid approaches combining atomic placement with self-assembly
pathway.unlocks: gram-scale materials with unprecedented purity and strength.
manufacturing of defect-free materials for aerospace, electronics and energy.
